providerClassifications.rule: Port deterministic orchestration, selection, normalization, finding/candidate separation, coverage accounting, and report semantics to Rust. Their current source-language modules are not a target runtime boundary.

providerClassifications.targetOwner: Arcane-gated external-project-tool executor called by Legion Rust core
providerClassifications.rule: A target repository tool is an intentional typed request, not a Legion runtime dependency. Require policy authorization immediately before the effect, an argument-bounded non-shell invocation, executable identity/provenance, timeout/output/cancellation bounds, immutable raw output, process-tree control, and a receipt; unavailable or denied tooling is truthful typed degradation.

providerClassifications.targetOwner: Agent client/host reviewer service with Legion Rust contract adapter
providerClassifications.rule: Model invocation and native host tools stay host-owned. Legion passes a typed bounded packet and preserves unavailable/invalid service outcomes as unproven; host service output cannot self-certify or close its own finding.

These historical runtime-registry rows are retained as source evidence only; each algorithm ports to Rust or is explicitly retired by a later ownership packet. They cannot remain a Node runtime fallback.

declarativeRule.owner: Versioned Legion assets consumed by Rust
includes: skills, prompts, lenses, recipes, and rule packs
declarativeRule.rule: Data declares semantics but does not execute Legion-owned algorithmic workflows. Rust validates and interprets the data under the frozen contracts.

blueprint.owner: Membrane typed interface and Blueprint repository-truth service
blueprint.appliesTo: Every provider whose current record consumes blueprint-packet, including all 63 rows in src/registry/providers.json and all 7 rows in src/registry/providers-runtime.json.
blueprint.rule: Blueprint supplies context/evidence, never a global runtime gate. A non-Blueprint-capable provider runs when applicable and reports exact structural-coverage loss; an explicitly Blueprint-dependent operation returns a provider-level typed degradation. Legion does not synthesize local graph truth.

hostServices.owner: Agent client/host, Membrane, Blueprint, Cortex, OmniRouter, or declared external capability
hostServices.rule: Host services are never silently emulated by Legion. Each has declared probe/remedy/degradation behavior; unavailability remains visible and cannot be coerced to empty success.

providerExecutionInvariants: No selected provider is unowned or has two semantic owners.
Provider selection, dependency closure, denominators, findings, candidates, coverage gaps, degradation, and receipts are deterministic Legion Rust responsibilities.
Candidate generators cannot emit or close findings; independent adjudication remains separate.
No provider reports successful empty output for an unavailable service or tool.
Blueprint unavailability cannot block non-Blueprint providers or erase their selected-provider denominator.
External project tools do not make Node, Python, shell, Cargo, or other project executables Legion runtime dependencies.
